- If sentiment is positive (≥ 0.33) in recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; reduce forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- If sentiment is negative (≤ -0.33), model often underestimates; increase forecast by 1–3% for next 5–10 days.  
- After a sharp price spike (forecast > 85), model frequently overcorrects downward; cap downward movement at 5–7% below peak for 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days below 75), model often fails to recognize it; adjust downward by 1–2% per day until trend stabilizes.  
- If model forecast is consistently 5–10% above true outcome over 3–5 days, apply a “lag correction” — reduce forecast by 2–4% for next 3–7 days.  
- If sentiment is mixed or neutral (0.00–0.33), model often overreacts; apply a “sentiment dampener” — reduce forecast by 1–2% for next 3–5 days.  
- If true outcome shows a sharp drop after a spike, model often fails to anticipate; add a “drop buffer” — reduce forecast by 3–5% for next 2–4 days.
